1.description: Chickadees visiting feeders in small flocks, their cheerful "chick-a-dee-dee-dee" call breaking winter silence
1.childFriendlyNote: A tiny brave bird with a black cap calls its own name: "chick-a-dee-dee-dee!" Count the dees!

1.description: Bold blue jays at feeders and caching seeds in snow, bright flash of blue against white landscape
1.childFriendlyNote: A bright blue bird with a spiky crest screams "jay jay!" and stuffs seeds into its throat pouch like pockets

1.description: Fresh tracks of cottontail rabbits, red foxes, and white-tailed deer visible in new snow
1.childFriendlyNote: Snow is like a giant white notebook. Animals write their stories with their feet! Can you follow them?

1.description: Brilliant red male cardinals at feeders, standing out vividly against white snow
1.childFriendlyNote: The reddest bird you ever saw sits on a snowy branch like a little Christmas decoration that stayed behind

1.description: Tiny woodpeckers tapping on branches and visiting suet feeders, black and white with a red spot on males
1.childFriendlyNote: Tap-tap-tap! A little black-and-white bird hammers on a tree like a tiny drummer looking for bugs

1.description: Feisty red squirrels raiding bird feeders and chattering angrily from spruce branches
1.childFriendlyNote: A little rusty-red squirrel scolds you from a branch. It chatters so fast it sounds like a tiny alarm clock!

2.description: Chickadees foraging in small flocks, sometimes beginning their spring "fee-bee" whistle on mild days
2.childFriendlyNote: A tiny brave bird with a black cap calls its own name: "chick-a-dee-dee-dee!" Count the dees!

2.description: Great horned owls hooting in courtship duets at dusk, one of the earliest nesting birds in Canada
2.childFriendlyNote: At night, a deep "hoo-hoo-hoooo" echoes through the trees. A huge owl with ear tufts is singing a love song!

2.description: Cardinals at feeders in pairs, the female a warm tawny-brown with red tinges
2.childFriendlyNote: The reddest bird you ever saw sits on a snowy branch like a little Christmas decoration that stayed behind

2.description: Deer tracks and trails in deep snow, deer yarding up in sheltered hemlock stands to survive winter
2.childFriendlyNote: Heart-shaped hoofprints in the snow! Follow them carefully and you might spot a deer hiding in the evergreens

2.description: Red squirrels active on milder days, digging through snow to find cached cones
2.childFriendlyNote: A little rusty-red squirrel scolds you from a branch. It chatters so fast it sounds like a tiny alarm clock!

3.description: Great horned owls nesting now, sitting on eggs in freezing temperatures in old hawk or crow nests
3.childFriendlyNote: A huge fluffy owl sits on her eggs in the snow. She keeps them warm with her feathery blanket body!

3.description: Chickadees beginning their clear two-note "fee-bee" spring song on sunny mornings
3.childFriendlyNote: The chickadee has a new song! Instead of its name, it whistles "fee-bee", like it's calling spring to come

3.description: Blue jays noisy at feeders, sometimes mimicking hawk calls to scare other birds away
3.childFriendlyNote: Sneaky blue jays pretend to be hawks. They copy the hawk's scream to scare everyone off the feeder!

3.description: Hairy woodpeckers drumming on resonant dead trees, establishing territory with rapid-fire beats
3.childFriendlyNote: A woodpecker drums so fast on a dead tree it sounds like a tiny jackhammer. That's how it says "this is my tree!"

3.description: Cottontail rabbit tracks in snow, distinctive paired prints where hind feet land ahead of front
3.childFriendlyNote: Two big footprints in front of two small ones. That's a bunny! Its back feet jump over its front feet every hop

4.description: Great horned owls incubating eggs, males hunting to feed the sitting female
4.childFriendlyNote: A huge fluffy owl sits on her eggs in the snow. She keeps them warm with her feathery blanket body!

4.description: Chickadees whistling "fee-bee" regularly, a sure sign that daylight is lengthening
4.childFriendlyNote: The chickadee has a new song! Instead of its name, it whistles "fee-bee", like it's calling spring to come

4.description: Male cardinals beginning to sing their loud "birdy-birdy-birdy" whistle from treetops at dawn
4.childFriendlyNote: A bright red bird sits on the tippy-top of a tree and sings "birdy birdy birdy" to wake up the whole neighbourhood!

4.description: Nuthatches walking headfirst down tree trunks, their nasal "yank yank" call carrying through bare woods
4.childFriendlyNote: This bird walks down the tree headfirst like a little acrobat. No other bird does that!

4.description: Crow-sized woodpeckers hammering rectangular holes in dead trees, wood chips scattered on snow below
4.childFriendlyNote: A giant woodpecker with a red mohawk smashes square holes in trees. Look for wood chips on the snow below!

5.description: Chickadees singing "fee-bee" with increasing frequency as days lengthen toward February's end
5.childFriendlyNote: The chickadee has a new song! Instead of its name, it whistles "fee-bee", like it's calling spring to come

5.description: Owlets may be hatching in early nests, parents bringing prey to the nest
5.childFriendlyNote: Baby owls are hatching in the freezing cold! Their fluffy white down keeps them warm as toast

5.description: Red foxes in breeding season, tracks paired in snow as mates travel together, barking calls at night
5.childFriendlyNote: Two sets of fox footprints walk side by side in the snow: a boy fox and a girl fox are falling in love!

5.description: Flocks of tiny redpolls at feeders, small streaky finches with a red cap and pink chest
5.childFriendlyNote: A flock of tiny birds with red polka-dot heads swarms the feeder. They flew down from the Arctic!

5.description: Deer browsing on cedar and hemlock in deep snow, winter coats thick and grey
5.childFriendlyNote: Deer nibble on evergreen branches when snow covers all the other food. Their grey winter coats are like warm woolly jumpers

6.description: Crows becoming more vocal, gathering in noisy groups as days lengthen
6.childFriendlyNote: Big black crows are getting loud. They caw and caw like they have exciting news to share with everyone!

6.description: Chickadees "fee-bee" song heard daily, pairs beginning to explore potential nest cavities
6.childFriendlyNote: Chickadee pairs are house-hunting! They peek into little holes in trees looking for the perfect home

6.description: Downy woodpeckers drumming on trees and utility poles to establish territory
6.childFriendlyNote: Tap-tap-tap! A little black-and-white bird hammers on a tree like a tiny drummer looking for bugs

6.description: Red squirrels chasing each other through branches in early mating season, chattering loudly
6.childFriendlyNote: Red squirrels race through the treetops playing chase. They're so fast they look like fuzzy red bouncy balls!

6.description: Mourning doves cooing softly at feeders, their gentle "coo-oo, coo, coo" carrying on still mornings
6.childFriendlyNote: A soft grey bird sings "coo-ooo, coo, coo". It sounds sad but it's actually a happy love song!

7.description: Horned larks appearing on bare patches of plowed fields, one of the earliest spring migrants
7.childFriendlyNote: A little bird with tiny black horns walks on bare, frosty ground, one of the bravest birds to come back first!

7.description: Cardinals singing loudly at dawn, staking out territory as breeding season approaches
7.childFriendlyNote: A bright red bird sits on the tippy-top of a tree and sings "birdy birdy birdy" to wake up the whole neighbourhood!

7.description: Chickadee pairs inspecting tree cavities and old woodpecker holes for nesting
7.childFriendlyNote: Chickadee pairs are house-hunting! They peek into little holes in trees looking for the perfect home

7.description: Red-tailed hawks soaring and calling with raspy screams, beginning courtship sky-dances
7.childFriendlyNote: A big hawk circles high in the sky and screams "keee-aaaah!". That's the sound you hear in every movie!

7.description: Grey squirrels chasing each other in courtship, leaping acrobatically between bare branches
7.childFriendlyNote: Grey squirrels play tag through the treetops, jumping from branch to branch without ever falling!

8.description: Crow flocks breaking up into pairs as they begin nest-building in tall trees
8.childFriendlyNote: Crows fly around carrying sticks in their beaks. They're building big messy nests at the tops of the tallest trees!

8.description: Juncos still at feeders, dark grey with white belly flash when they fly, flocks on the ground under feeders
8.childFriendlyNote: Little grey birds hop under the feeder picking up dropped seeds. When they fly, their tails flash white like tiny signals!

8.description: First male red-winged blackbirds returning to wetland edges, singing "conk-la-ree!" from cattails
8.childFriendlyNote: A shiny black bird flashes bright red shoulder patches and sings "conk-la-ree!". Spring is on its way!

8.description: Cardinal pairs becoming more visible, male feeding seeds to female in courtship
8.childFriendlyNote: The boy cardinal picks up a seed and gently puts it in the girl cardinal's beak. That's a birdy kiss!

8.description: Pussy willow buds swelling on streamside shrubs, soft silver catkins just beginning to peek out
8.childFriendlyNote: Soft silver bumps on willow branches feel like tiny kitten paws. That's why they're called pussy willows!

9.description: More male red-winged blackbirds arriving, defending cattail territories with loud displays
9.childFriendlyNote: A shiny black bird flashes bright red shoulder patches and sings "conk-la-ree!". Spring is on its way!

9.description: Pussy willow catkins fully emerged, soft furry silver ovals glowing along streambanks
9.childFriendlyNote: Soft silver bumps on willow branches feel like tiny kitten paws. That's why they're called pussy willows!

9.description: Crows returning in large numbers, noisy flocks gathering at dusk in communal roosts
9.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of crows fly to one big tree at sunset. It's like a crow sleepover party every night!

9.description: Maple sap starting to run as nights freeze and days thaw, the start of sugaring season across Quebec and Ontario
9.childFriendlyNote: When it's freezing at night and warm in the day, sweet water drips from maple trees. People boil it into yummy syrup!

9.description: Juncos still present in good numbers, trilling their musical song on sunny mornings
9.childFriendlyNote: Little grey birds hop under the feeder picking up dropped seeds. When they fly, their tails flash white like tiny signals!

9.description: Tiny black springtails appearing on snow surface on warm days, looking like scattered pepper
9.childFriendlyNote: Look at the snow. It's covered in tiny black specks that jump! They're called snow fleas but they don't bite!

10.description: Peak maple syrup season, sap flowing freely, sugar shacks boiling sap across Ontario and Quebec
10.childFriendlyNote: Steam pours from sugar shacks and the air smells like pancakes! It takes 40 buckets of sap to make one bucket of syrup

10.description: Red-winged blackbirds in full song at every marsh and pond edge, a chorus of "conk-la-ree" calls
10.childFriendlyNote: A shiny black bird flashes bright red shoulder patches and sings "conk-la-ree!". Spring is really here!

10.description: Pussy willows in full bloom, catkins turning gold with pollen on sunny days
10.childFriendlyNote: The fuzzy silver kitten-paw buds are turning golden and dusty with pollen. Bees love them!

10.description: Snow fleas active on warm afternoons, thousands of tiny springtails bouncing on snow near tree bases
10.childFriendlyNote: Look at the snow. It's covered in tiny black specks that jump! They're called snow fleas but they don't bite!

10.description: First robins spotted on lawns with bare patches, a classic sign of spring across Eastern Canada
10.childFriendlyNote: A plump bird with a rusty-red tummy hops across the lawn. When you see a robin, spring is knocking on the door!

10.description: Grackles returning in noisy flocks, iridescent black plumage gleaming purple and green in the sun
10.childFriendlyNote: A big black bird that looks plain suddenly turns shiny purple and green in the sunlight, like a magic trick!

11.description: Maple syrup season continuing, sap buckets and tubing lines visible throughout hardwood forests
11.childFriendlyNote: Steam pours from sugar shacks and the air smells like pancakes! It takes 40 buckets of sap to make one bucket of syrup

11.description: Robins arriving in waves, flocks feeding on last year's crabapples and berries
11.childFriendlyNote: A plump bird with a rusty-red tummy hops across the lawn. When you see a robin, spring is knocking on the door!

11.description: Female red-winged blackbirds now arriving to join males at marshes, streaky brown and hard to spot
11.childFriendlyNote: The girl red-winged blackbirds arrive at last. They're sneaky brown so they can hide their nest in the cattails

11.description: Song sparrows returning and singing their bright, complex song from shrubs and fence posts
11.childFriendlyNote: A streaky brown bird sits on a bush and sings the prettiest, bounciest tune. Every song sparrow has its own special version!

11.description: Grackle flocks growing, their creaky-gate calls filling parking lots and parks
11.childFriendlyNote: A big black bird that looks plain suddenly turns shiny purple and green in the sunlight, like a magic trick!

12.description: Late maple syrup season, sap runs slowing as buds begin to swell on maple branches
12.childFriendlyNote: Syrup season is ending. The maple buds are swelling and that changes the taste of the sap. Time for the last pancake party!

12.description: Robins now widespread, singing their cheerful "cheerily, cheer-up, cheerio" song at dawn
12.childFriendlyNote: Robins are the alarm clocks of spring! They start singing "cheerily, cheer-up!" before you even wake up

12.description: Canada geese returning in V-formations, loud honking heard overhead as flocks fly north
12.childFriendlyNote: Look up! A big V of honking geese flies north. They take turns at the front because leading is hard work

12.description: Red-tailed hawks performing dramatic courtship flights, diving and swooping together
12.childFriendlyNote: Two big hawks hold hands with their claws way up in the sky and tumble down together: it's a love dance in the air!

12.description: Song sparrows singing strongly from every hedgerow and stream edge
12.childFriendlyNote: A streaky brown bird sits on a bush and sings the prettiest, bounciest tune. Every song sparrow has its own special version!

12.description: Killdeer returning to open fields and gravel areas, running and calling their loud "kill-deer" cry
12.childFriendlyNote: A bird runs across the field screaming its own name: "kill-deer! kill-deer!" If you get close, it pretends its wing is broken to trick you away from its nest!

13.description: Geese settling on ponds and parks, pairs establishing nesting territories near water
13.childFriendlyNote: Canada geese honk and hiss to guard their spot. Don't get too close, the parents are fierce protectors!

13.description: Robins pulling earthworms from thawing lawns, head-tilting to listen for worms underground
13.childFriendlyNote: Watch the robin tilt its head and listen... then yank! It pulls a wiggly worm right out of the ground!

13.description: Red-winged blackbird males in full territorial display, puffing up red epaulets on cattail stalks
13.childFriendlyNote: The blackbird puffs out his red shoulder patches like little flags and sings as loud as he can: "look at me!"

13.description: Mourning cloak butterflies emerging from hibernation on warm days, dark wings edged in gold
13.childFriendlyNote: A big dark butterfly with a golden edge floats through the still-bare woods. It slept under bark all winter long!

13.description: Silver maples blooming with tiny red flowers before any leaves appear, one of the earliest flowering trees
13.childFriendlyNote: The bare silver maple tree is covered in tiny red fuzzy flowers. It's blooming before any leaves! Bees love it

13.description: Song sparrows singing from every shrub and fencepost, one of the most common spring sounds
13.childFriendlyNote: A streaky brown bird sits on a bush and sings the prettiest, bounciest tune. Every song sparrow has its own special version!

14.description: Geese nesting near ponds and rivers, females sitting on nests while males stand guard
14.childFriendlyNote: The mother goose sits on her big nest while the father stands guard. He'll hiss if you come too close!

14.description: Robins building cup-shaped mud nests in sheltered spots, carrying beakfuls of mud and grass
14.childFriendlyNote: The robin is a little builder! It makes a mud cup and lines it with soft grass: a perfect bowl for bright blue eggs

14.description: Lake ice becoming grey and honeycombed, cracks and open leads forming near shore, early ice-out beginning
14.childFriendlyNote: The lake ice is cracking and groaning. It sounds like a giant is stretching! Soon the whole lake will be water again

14.description: Red maples blooming with clusters of tiny scarlet flowers, giving a red haze to swampy woodland edges
14.childFriendlyNote: The bare trees suddenly look like they're blushing! Tiny red flowers cover the red maple before any leaves come out

14.description: Killdeer nesting in gravel areas and playing fields, performing broken-wing display if disturbed
14.childFriendlyNote: A bird runs across the field screaming its own name: "kill-deer!" If you get close, it fakes a broken wing to lead you away from its nest!

14.description: Ring-billed gulls returning to parking lots and fast-food restaurants, a sure urban sign of spring
14.childFriendlyNote: Seagulls are back in the parking lots! They're actually ring-billed gulls and they love french fries

15.description: Spring peepers beginning to call from woodland ponds, a high-pitched chorus of "peep peep peep" at dusk
15.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of tiny tree frogs the size of your thumbnail scream "peep! peep!" so loud you can hear them from the road!

15.description: Lake ice breaking up rapidly, open water expanding, loons and ducks arriving on newly open water
15.childFriendlyNote: The ice is breaking into jigsaw pieces and floating away. The lake is waking up from its long winter sleep!

15.description: Hepatica flowers pushing through dead leaves on forest floor, fuzzy stems with delicate pink, white, or blue blooms
15.childFriendlyNote: Tiny flowers in pink, blue, or white push right up through dead leaves. They're so eager for spring they can't wait!

15.description: Red maples in full flower, swamps and streamsides glowing with crimson bloom against bare grey woods
15.childFriendlyNote: The swampy woods look like they're on fire, but it's just millions of tiny red maple flowers!

15.description: Geese sitting tight on nests, males aggressively guarding, hissing at passersby
15.childFriendlyNote: The father goose stretches his neck and hisses if you walk near. He's protecting the eggs like a feathery security guard!

15.description: Mourning cloak butterflies basking on sun-warmed tree trunks and paths on mild days
15.childFriendlyNote: A big dark butterfly opens its wings to sunbathe on a warm tree trunk. It survived the whole winter hiding under bark!

16.description: Peeper chorus now deafening at dusk near woodland ponds, one of the defining sounds of Canadian spring
16.childFriendlyNote: The peeper frogs are so loud now you almost have to shout! Each tiny frog is only as big as a grape

16.description: Bloodroot flowering on forest floor, each white flower wrapped in a single curled leaf like a cape
16.childFriendlyNote: A pure white flower wears a green leaf wrapped around it like a superhero cape. Break the stem and it bleeds orange!

16.description: Wood frogs calling from vernal pools with a quacking sound, mating in temporary spring ponds
16.childFriendlyNote: Frogs that sound like ducks! Wood frogs go "quack quack quack" from muddy puddles in the forest. But they're frogs!

16.description: Robins laying bright blue eggs, males singing at dawn from every neighbourhood treetop
16.childFriendlyNote: Robin eggs are the most beautiful blue you've ever seen, like the sky painted tiny and put in a nest!

16.description: Red maple flowers fading, tiny winged seed pairs (samaras) beginning to form
16.childFriendlyNote: The red maple flowers are turning into little helicopter seeds. Spin them in the air and watch them twirl down!

16.description: Tree swallows returning, iridescent blue-green backs flashing as they swoop over ponds catching insects
16.childFriendlyNote: Shiny blue-green birds zoom and swoop over the pond like little fighter jets catching bugs in mid-air!

17.description: Bloodroot in peak flower, white petals opening wide on warm days, closing at night
17.childFriendlyNote: The white bloodroot flowers open in sunshine and close at night. They go to sleep just like you do!

17.description: First trilliums emerging on forest floor, Ontario's provincial flower beginning to bloom in southern areas
17.childFriendlyNote: Three leaves, three white petals. Everything about the trillium comes in threes! It's Ontario's special flower

17.description: Spring peeper chorus at full volume, hundreds of males calling together from every pond and ditch
17.childFriendlyNote: The peeper frogs are so loud now you almost have to shout! Each tiny frog is only as big as a grape

17.description: Sapsuckers returning, drilling neat rows of tiny holes in birch and maple bark to lick sap
17.childFriendlyNote: This woodpecker drills tiny holes in neat rows like a dotted line, then licks up the sweet tree sap like a lollipop!

17.description: Chipmunks emerging from hibernation, scurrying over forest floor and stone walls, cheeks already stuffing
17.childFriendlyNote: The chipmunks are awake! They stuff their cheeks so full of seeds they look like furry little balloons with stripes

18.description: Trilliums spreading across forest floors, white blooms glowing in dappled spring sunlight
18.childFriendlyNote: The forest floor is covered in white three-petaled flowers like a carpet of stars under the trees!

18.description: Wild leeks carpeting rich hardwood forest floors, broad green leaves with a strong garlic-onion smell
18.childFriendlyNote: The forest smells like garlic bread! Wild leeks are like onions that grow in the woods. Bears love eating them

18.description: Tiny kinglets passing through on migration, constantly flicking their wings and singing a surprisingly loud song
18.childFriendlyNote: One of the tiniest birds in the world sings one of the loudest songs. It flicks its wings like it's so excited it can't sit still!

18.description: Wood frog eggs visible in vernal pools, large jelly masses with black embryos developing
18.childFriendlyNote: Look in the forest puddles. Big blobs of clear jelly with black dots are baby frogs growing! Each dot will be a tadpole

18.description: Sapsuckers actively drilling sap wells, hummingbirds and other birds visiting the oozing holes
18.childFriendlyNote: The sapsucker's holes are like tiny drinking fountains. Other birds come to sip the sweet sap too!

18.description: Chipmunks fully active, chipping alarm calls from stone walls and stumps when they spot predators
18.childFriendlyNote: The chipmunks are awake! They stuff their cheeks so full of seeds they look like furry little balloons with stripes

19.description: Trilliums at peak, entire forest floors glowing white, older flowers turning pink as they age
19.childFriendlyNote: The white trilliums are blushing pink as they get old. It's like the forest floor changes colour right before your eyes!

19.description: First wave of warblers arriving: yellow warblers, black-and-white warblers, and palm warblers in treetops
19.childFriendlyNote: Tiny colourful birds are arriving from far away! They hop through the treetops so fast you need binoculars to see them

19.description: First Baltimore orioles arriving, brilliant orange and black males singing from tall elms and maples
19.childFriendlyNote: A bird as orange as a tangerine arrives from the tropics! Put out orange halves and it might visit your garden

19.description: Jack-in-the-pulpit flowers emerging on forest floor, the hooded green and purple spathe curving over the spadix
19.childFriendlyNote: A tiny person stands in a stripy green-and-purple tent. That's Jack in his pulpit! It's one of the weirdest flowers ever

19.description: Wild leeks at peak, broad leaves carpet the forest floor with a pungent onion-garlic scent
19.childFriendlyNote: The forest smells like garlic bread! Wild leeks are like onions that grow in the woods. Bears love eating them

19.description: First ruby-throated hummingbirds arriving, buzzing at early flowers and feeders
19.childFriendlyNote: A bird the size of your thumb hovers in the air like a tiny helicopter. Its wings beat 80 times every second!

20.description: Peak warbler migration: magnolia, blackburnian, chestnut-sided, and dozens more species passing through
20.childFriendlyNote: The trees are full of tiny colourful birds from the tropics! Yellow ones, stripy ones, orange ones. It's a bird rainbow!

20.description: Orioles now common, males whistling rich flute-like songs, females building hanging pouch nests
20.childFriendlyNote: The oriole weaves a hanging basket nest from plant fibres. It dangles from a branch like a little sock!

20.description: Lilacs beginning to bloom, purple and white flower clusters filling the air with sweet scent
20.childFriendlyNote: Big bunches of purple flowers smell so sweet. Push your nose right in and take a big sniff of lilac perfume!

20.description: Hummingbirds visiting columbine flowers and sugar-water feeders, males flashing red throat in display
20.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbird's throat flashes bright red like a jewel when the sun hits it. Then it looks black! Magic!

20.description: Apple trees coming into bloom, pink buds opening to white-and-pink flowers, buzzing with pollinators
20.childFriendlyNote: Apple trees look like they're covered in pink-and-white popcorn. Every flower will try to become an apple!

21.description: Late wave warblers arriving: bay-breasted, Wilson's, and Canada warblers among the last to pass through
21.childFriendlyNote: The last of the tiny tropical birds are zooming through. Some are heading even further north to the boreal forest!

21.description: Lilacs at peak bloom, the sweet fragrance drifting across gardens and old farmsteads
21.childFriendlyNote: Big bunches of purple flowers smell so sweet. Push your nose right in and take a big sniff of lilac perfume!

21.description: Apple orchards in full bloom, air heavy with sweet scent, bees working every flower
21.childFriendlyNote: The whole apple orchard buzzes with bees visiting every single flower, no bees, no apples!

21.description: Painted turtles basking on logs in ponds, stacking on top of each other in sunny spots
21.childFriendlyNote: Turtles line up on a log like they're waiting for a bus. Some even sit on top of each other to get the best sunshine!

21.description: Trilliums fading, white flowers turning deep pink and wilting, the spring show winding down
21.childFriendlyNote: The trilliums are turning pink and droopy. They danced all spring and now they're tired!

21.description: Hummingbirds established at territories, visiting columbine and bee balm flowers
21.childFriendlyNote: A bird the size of your thumb hovers in the air like a tiny helicopter. Its wings beat 80 times every second!

22.description: Loons returning to northern lakes, their haunting tremolo and yodel calls echoing across the water at dusk
22.childFriendlyNote: The most magical sound in Canada! A loon calls across the lake at sunset. It sounds like a wild, lonely laugh

22.description: Lilacs fading, brown spent flowers replacing the purple clusters
22.childFriendlyNote: The lilac flowers are turning brown and crispy. The sweet smell is fading until next spring

22.description: First fireflies appearing at dusk in meadows and garden edges, tiny yellow-green flashes
22.childFriendlyNote: Tiny flying lights blink on and off in the tall grass at bedtime. Fireflies are beetles that glow in the dark!

22.description: Wild roses opening pink blooms along roadsides and field edges, simple five-petalled flowers
22.childFriendlyNote: Pink wild roses pop open along the path. They smell sweet and each flower has exactly five petals like a star

22.description: Bright orange-red efts (juvenile newts) walking across forest floor after rain, toxic skin warns predators
22.childFriendlyNote: After rain, bright orange baby newts walk across the forest floor like tiny neon lizards. Their colour says "don't eat me!"

23.description: Loons nesting on lakeshores, their wild tremolo call carrying across still water at dawn and dusk
23.childFriendlyNote: The most magical sound in Canada! A loon calls across the lake at sunset. It sounds like a wild, lonely laugh

23.description: Fireflies increasing, meadows and gardens twinkling with yellow-green flashes at dusk
23.childFriendlyNote: The meadow is full of little flying stars! Each firefly blinks its own pattern to find a friend

23.description: Milkweed plants growing tall, round pink flower buds forming, the only food for monarch caterpillars
23.childFriendlyNote: The milkweed plant is getting tall. Snap a leaf and white milky sap oozes out! Monarchs need this plant to survive

23.description: Painted turtles basking on every available log, females beginning to leave ponds to lay eggs in sandy soil
23.childFriendlyNote: Mama turtle digs a hole in sandy ground with her back feet, lays her eggs, covers them up, and walks away. The babies are on their own!

23.description: Wild roses in full bloom along fencerows and roadsides, attracting bees and butterflies
23.childFriendlyNote: Pink wild roses pop open along the path. They smell sweet and each flower has exactly five petals like a star

23.description: Barn swallows swooping in and out of barns and sheds, building mud nests on beams and rafters
23.childFriendlyNote: Sleek blue-and-orange birds zoom in and out of barns carrying mud in their beaks to build little cup nests on the wall!

24.description: Loon pairs on nests at lake edges, taking turns incubating while the other fishes nearby
24.childFriendlyNote: The loon sits on its nest right at the water's edge. It can barely walk on land but it's the best swimmer on the lake!

24.description: Firefly displays at peak, fields and gardens lit up with synchronizing flashes at dusk
24.childFriendlyNote: The meadow is full of little flying stars! Each firefly blinks its own pattern to find a friend

24.description: Milkweed flowers opening, pink globes of sweet-scented blooms attracting bees and butterflies
24.childFriendlyNote: The milkweed has pink ball-shaped flowers that smell like honey. Bees, butterflies, and beetles all crowd around!

24.description: White birch dangling green catkins, papery bark peeling in curls on the distinctive white trunks
24.childFriendlyNote: White birch bark peels off in papery curls you can write on. Indigenous peoples made canoes from this amazing bark!

24.description: Dragonflies patrolling over ponds and streams, darners and skimmers hawking insects over open water
24.childFriendlyNote: Dragonflies zoom over the water like tiny helicopters. They can fly forwards, backwards, and even hover! And they eat mosquitoes!

25.description: Loon chicks hatching, tiny black puffballs riding on parents' backs across the lake
25.childFriendlyNote: Baby loons ride on their mum's back like tiny black fluffballs on a boat. They're too small to swim alone yet!

25.description: First monarch butterflies arriving from the south, females searching for milkweed to lay eggs
25.childFriendlyNote: An orange-and-black butterfly arrives after flying thousands of kilometres from Mexico! She's looking for milkweed for her babies

25.description: Milkweed in full flower, round pink clusters buzzing with pollinators, strong sweet fragrance
25.childFriendlyNote: The milkweed has pink ball-shaped flowers that smell like honey. Bees, butterflies, and beetles all crowd around!

25.description: Tiny wild strawberries ripening in sunny meadows and forest edges, intensely sweet flavour
25.childFriendlyNote: Tiny red strawberries hide in the grass. They're smaller than your thumbnail but taste ten times sweeter than shop ones!

25.description: Dragonflies abundant over ponds and meadows, aerial hunters catching mosquitoes and midges
25.childFriendlyNote: Dragonflies zoom over the water like tiny helicopters. They can fly forwards, backwards, and even hover! And they eat mosquitoes!

26.description: Loon families on lakes, parents diving for fish to feed growing chicks
26.childFriendlyNote: Baby loons ride on their mum's back like tiny black fluffballs on a boat. They're learning to dive for fish!

26.description: Peak firefly season, warm humid evenings bringing spectacular displays in meadows
26.childFriendlyNote: On warm evenings the whole meadow twinkles like a fairy kingdom. Hundreds of fireflies flash their lights!

26.description: Monarch butterflies laying eggs on milkweed undersides, tiny white eggs visible with careful looking
26.childFriendlyNote: Flip over a milkweed leaf. Do you see a tiny white pearl? That's a monarch egg! A caterpillar will hatch in a few days

26.description: Beaver activity visible at dusk: V-shaped wakes on ponds, freshly gnawed trees, dam maintenance
26.childFriendlyNote: Look for pointy tree stumps near the water. A beaver chewed them down! At sunset you might see one swimming with a branch in its mouth

26.description: Wild blueberry flowers fading, tiny green berries forming on low bushes in rocky and sandy areas
26.childFriendlyNote: Tiny green balls are growing where the blueberry flowers were. They'll turn blue and delicious in a few weeks!

26.description: Peak summer: long warm days, lush green forests, lakes warm enough for swimming, full chorus of birdsong at dawn
26.childFriendlyNote: Happy Canada Day! Summer is here. The days are so long, the lakes are warm, and everything is green green green!

27.description: Loon families feeding on lakes, chicks growing rapidly, parents teaching them to dive
27.childFriendlyNote: Baby loons are learning to dive under the water. They go down for a second then pop right back up like corks!

27.description: Monarch caterpillars feeding on milkweed, yellow, white, and black striped larvae munching leaves
27.childFriendlyNote: A fat stripy caterpillar in yellow, white, and black munches milkweed leaves. It's going to become a butterfly!

27.description: Wild blueberries beginning to ripen on rocky ridges and forest edges, green turning to dusty blue
27.childFriendlyNote: The first blueberries are turning blue! Pop one in your mouth. Wild ones are tiny but so much sweeter than shop ones

27.description: Great blue herons standing motionless in shallows, lightning-fast strikes to catch fish and frogs
27.childFriendlyNote: A bird as tall as you stands perfectly still in the water... then stab! Its long beak catches a fish faster than you can blink!

27.description: Peak dragonfly season: blue darners, red skimmers, and green-eyed clubtails patrolling every waterway
27.childFriendlyNote: Dragonflies zoom over the water like tiny helicopters. They can fly forwards, backwards, and even hover! And they eat mosquitoes!

28.description: Wild blueberries ripening, bushes heavy with dusty-blue fruit on rocky outcrops and forest edges
28.childFriendlyNote: Blueberry picking time! Your fingers and tongue turn purple-blue and the berries burst with sweetness in your mouth

28.description: Monarch caterpillars growing large on milkweed, some forming jade-green chrysalises with gold dots
28.childFriendlyNote: The caterpillar hangs upside down and turns into a beautiful green jewel box with real gold dots, a chrysalis! A butterfly is growing inside

28.description: Loon chicks half-grown, still riding on parents' backs occasionally, diving for short periods
28.childFriendlyNote: The loon babies are getting bigger. They can dive under the water now but still like hitching a ride on mum's back!

28.description: Beavers active at dusk, kits (young) visible swimming near the lodge, loud tail slaps warning of danger
28.childFriendlyNote: Slap! A beaver smacks its flat tail on the water to say "danger!" The sound is like a gunshot and all the beavers dive!

28.description: Herons fishing at dawn and dusk, prehistoric-looking silhouette standing still in shallows
28.childFriendlyNote: A bird as tall as you stands perfectly still in the water... then stab! Its long beak catches a fish faster than you can blink!

29.description: Peak wild blueberry season, bears and birds competing with human pickers on rocky barrens
29.childFriendlyNote: Blueberry picking time! Your fingers and tongue turn purple-blue and the berries burst with sweetness in your mouth

29.description: New-generation monarchs emerging from chrysalises, fresh orange-and-black wings drying in the sun
29.childFriendlyNote: A brand new butterfly crawls out of its green chrysalis and unfolds crumpled wet wings. In an hour it will fly!

29.description: Nighthawks swooping over cities and fields at dusk, catching insects with wide gaping mouths
29.childFriendlyNote: At sunset, a bird with long pointy wings swoops through the sky eating bugs. It has a mouth so wide it's like a flying butterfly net!

29.description: Cicadas buzzing from treetops, their loud droning hum the signature sound of hot July days
29.childFriendlyNote: A loud buzzing comes from the trees. It's a cicada! It lived underground for years and now it's singing its heart out in the sun

29.description: Bullfrogs calling from ponds and marshes, deep "jug-o-rum" bass notes carrying across the water
29.childFriendlyNote: A frog as big as your hand goes "jug-o-rum!" in a voice so deep and rumbly it sounds like a grumpy old man!

30.description: Monarch butterflies nectaring on milkweed and wildflowers, second generation breeding on milkweed
30.childFriendlyNote: Orange-and-black monarchs flutter between flowers sipping nectar. They're making the next batch of babies now!

30.description: Cicadas in full chorus, empty brown shells clinging to tree bark where they emerged
30.childFriendlyNote: Find a perfect see-through bug shell stuck to a tree. The cicada crawled out of its own skin! Keep it as a treasure

30.description: Goldenrod beginning to show yellow buds along roadsides and meadows, a preview of late summer
30.childFriendlyNote: Tall plants with fuzzy yellow tops are getting ready to bloom. Goldenrod means summer is halfway done!

30.description: Herons fishing actively, young herons learning to hunt in shallows, standing on gangly legs
30.childFriendlyNote: Teenage herons stand in the water on long wobbly legs. They miss the fish a lot more than their parents do!

30.description: Bullfrogs calling through warm nights, tadpoles visible in shallows of warm ponds
30.childFriendlyNote: A frog as big as your hand goes "jug-o-rum!" in a voice so deep and rumbly it sounds like a grumpy old man!

30.description: Loon chicks nearly half adult size, beginning to dive independently for small fish
30.childFriendlyNote: The loon chicks are growing fast. They can dive and catch tiny fish now, but they still peep for mum and dad!

31.description: Goldenrod beginning to bloom golden along roadsides, a magnet for pollinators
31.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy golden flowers are opening everywhere. Bees, beetles, and butterflies all crowd in for the sweet feast!

31.description: Second generation monarch caterpillars on milkweed, some already forming chrysalises
31.childFriendlyNote: The caterpillar hangs upside down and turns into a beautiful green jewel box with real gold dots. Magic is happening inside!

31.description: First purple asters opening along field edges, a preview of autumn's wildflower show
31.childFriendlyNote: Purple daisy-like flowers are starting to open. They're the last big feast for butterflies before autumn comes!

31.description: Cicadas buzzing loudly in afternoon heat, their metallic drone the soundtrack of August
31.childFriendlyNote: The louder the buzz from the treetops, the hotter the day! Cicadas are nature's thermometers

31.description: Nighthawks swooping over rooftops and ball fields at dusk, nasal "peent" calls overhead
31.childFriendlyNote: At sunset, a bird with long pointy wings swoops through the sky eating bugs. It has a mouth so wide it's like a flying butterfly net!

32.description: Goldenrod in full bloom, meadows and roadsides a sea of gold, alive with pollinators
32.childFriendlyNote: The meadow has turned golden! Bees, beetles, and butterflies all crowd the goldenrod like a buzzing party

32.description: Monarchs abundant, nectaring on goldenrod and asters, building fat reserves for the coming migration
32.childFriendlyNote: Monarchs are eating and eating and eating. They need lots of energy for their huge trip to Mexico soon!

32.description: Herons dispersing from breeding colonies, solitary birds fishing along every pond and stream
32.childFriendlyNote: A bird as tall as you stands perfectly still in the water... then stab! Its long beak catches a fish faster than you can blink!

32.description: Purple asters blooming strongly along roadsides and meadow edges, vital late-season pollinator food
32.childFriendlyNote: Purple daisy-like flowers are everywhere. Monarchs, bumblebees, and painted lady butterflies all love them!

32.description: Green frogs calling from pond edges, their banjo-string twang carrying across warm water
32.childFriendlyNote: A green frog goes "gunk!" like someone plucking a rubber band. It sounds like a banjo played by a frog!

33.description: Goldenrod at peak, paired with purple asters creating the classic late-summer golden-purple palette
33.childFriendlyNote: Gold and purple everywhere! Goldenrod and asters paint the meadow in the prettiest colour combo of the whole year

33.description: Late-season monarchs fattening on nectar, the migratory generation preparing for the flight to Mexico
33.childFriendlyNote: These monarchs were born to migrate! Unlike their parents, they'll live 8 months and fly all the way to Mexico

33.description: Cicadas still buzzing but less intense, a winding-down feel to the summer chorus
33.childFriendlyNote: The buzzing in the trees is getting quieter. The cicadas are winding down their summer songs

33.description: Nighthawks beginning to gather in loose flocks, early migrants heading south at dusk
33.childFriendlyNote: The nighthawks are leaving! Groups of them fly south at sunset, catching bugs all the way to South America

33.description: Dogwood berries ripening white on bright red stems along streams and wetland edges
33.childFriendlyNote: White berries on bright red sticks. Birds gobble them up but they're not for people! The red stems are beautiful in winter

34.description: Monarch migration beginning, butterflies drifting southward on favourable winds, pausing to nectar
34.childFriendlyNote: The monarchs are starting their incredible journey! They'll fly 4,000 km to a forest in Mexico they've never seen

34.description: Goldenrod starting to fade, some heads turning fluffy and going to seed
34.childFriendlyNote: The golden flowers are turning fluffy and brown. Each tiny seed has a parachute to float away on the wind!

34.description: Geese gathering in large flocks on playing fields and ponds, young birds now full-grown
34.childFriendlyNote: Huge flocks of geese munch grass on the sports field. The babies from spring are all grown up now!

34.description: Purple asters at peak bloom, the last great wildflower show before frost
34.childFriendlyNote: Purple daisy-like flowers are everywhere. They're the last big feast for butterflies before the cold comes!

34.description: Osprey families preparing to migrate, young birds making practice flights from the nest platform
34.childFriendlyNote: Young ospreys flap their wings on the nest like they're doing exercises. They're getting strong enough for their first big flight south!

35.description: Monarch migration in full swing, butterflies clustering on shorelines and in gardens during stopovers
35.childFriendlyNote: Monarch butterflies are heading south! Sometimes dozens rest together on one tree like orange leaves that flutter

35.description: Geese in restless flocks, short practice flights and increasing honking as migration urge builds
35.childFriendlyNote: The geese are getting fidgety! They honk and flap and fly short loops. They know it's almost time to head south

35.description: First hints of colour on sugar maples, scattered orange-red leaves appearing on stressed or exposed trees
35.childFriendlyNote: Look! A few maple leaves are turning orange already. It's like the trees are trying on their autumn costumes early

35.description: Chipmunks frantically gathering and caching nuts, cheek pouches bulging as they prepare for winter
35.childFriendlyNote: Chipmunks are busy! They stuff their cheeks until they look like furry balloons and race to hide food underground

35.description: Purple and pink asters still blooming strongly, supporting migrating butterflies and late-season bees
35.childFriendlyNote: Purple daisy-like flowers are everywhere, the last big feast for bees and butterflies before autumn

36.description: Sugar maples beginning to turn, patches of orange and scarlet appearing in the canopy, fall colour starting
36.childFriendlyNote: The sugar maples are starting their colour show! Green leaves are turning orange and red like someone's painting them

36.description: Late monarch migrants passing through, some gathering at Point Pelee and other lakeshores
36.childFriendlyNote: The last monarchs are heading south. Wave goodbye and wish them a safe trip to Mexico!

36.description: First goose V-formations heading south, honking calls overhead growing more frequent
36.childFriendlyNote: Look up! A big V of honking geese flies south. They take turns at the front because leading is hard work

36.description: Chipmunks in a frenzy of food caching, acorns and seeds stockpiled in underground burrows
36.childFriendlyNote: Chipmunks are busy! They stuff their cheeks until they look like furry balloons and race to hide food underground

36.description: First juncos returning from the north, a sign that winter birds are on the move
36.childFriendlyNote: The little grey "snowbirds" are coming back! When juncos show up at the feeder, cold weather is on its way

37.description: Sugar maples turning brilliant orange and scarlet, Eastern Canada's spectacular fall colour building rapidly
37.childFriendlyNote: The forests are turning into a painting! Sugar maples glow orange, red, and gold like they're on fire

37.description: Steady stream of goose flocks overhead in V-formation, honking their way south
37.childFriendlyNote: All day long, V after V of honking geese fly overhead. It's like a highway in the sky!

37.description: Red oaks turning deep russet and burgundy, acorns dropping and bouncing on paths
37.childFriendlyNote: Acorns rain down from the oak trees (bonk!) and squirrels race to grab them before anyone else can

37.description: White birch leaves turning bright gold, glowing against the white papery bark
37.childFriendlyNote: White birch trees look like golden coins hanging on white sticks. When the wind blows, the leaves shimmer and dance!

37.description: Chipmunks in overdrive, stuffing cheeks with acorns and seeds, short sharp alarm chips when disturbed
37.childFriendlyNote: Chipmunks are so busy gathering acorns they barely have time to scold you! Their cheeks are enormous

38.description: Sugar maple peak colour, hillsides ablaze with orange, red, and gold, one of nature's greatest shows
38.childFriendlyNote: The forests look like they're on fire with colour! Orange, red, gold. Sugar maples put on the best show in the whole world

38.description: Red oaks at peak colour, deep russet and burgundy leaves, heavy acorn drop on forest floor
38.childFriendlyNote: The oak trees turn dark red like wine. Their thick leathery leaves hold on longer than other trees

38.description: White birch at peak gold, leaves raining down in golden showers on windy days
38.childFriendlyNote: Golden birch leaves twirl down like little helicopters. Catch one before it hits the ground!

38.description: Large goose flocks staging on fields and ponds before continuing south, constant honking
38.childFriendlyNote: Thousands of geese cover the field like a honking carpet. They're resting before the next leg of their trip south

38.description: Juncos now common at feeders and in hedgerows, flashing white outer tail feathers
38.childFriendlyNote: The little grey "snowbirds" are back at the feeder! Their white tail flashes when they hop away

39.description: Sugar maples still stunning, some starting to shed, carpets of colourful leaves on forest floor
39.childFriendlyNote: Crunch through piles of colourful maple leaves! Kick them up and watch them swirl. The ground is as pretty as the trees

39.description: Red oaks holding their dark red and brown leaves while maples shed, acorn feast for squirrels
39.childFriendlyNote: The oak trees turn dark red like wine. Their thick leathery leaves hold on tight while other trees go bare

39.description: Thanksgiving weekend: pumpkins and squash ripe, apple harvest underway, last warm days before winter
39.childFriendlyNote: Happy Thanksgiving! Pumpkins are orange, apples are ready, and the air smells like cinnamon and leaves

39.description: Blue jays caching acorns for winter, burying them in lawns and garden beds, calling loudly
39.childFriendlyNote: Blue jays are hiding acorns everywhere! They bury thousands but forget some, and those grow into new oak trees!

39.description: White-throated sparrows migrating through, singing their haunting "Oh sweet Canada, Canada, Canada" whistle
39.childFriendlyNote: A little stripy bird whistles "Oh sweet Canada, Canada, Canada". It's the most Canadian birdsong there is!

40.description: Sugar maples past peak, many leaves fallen, bare branches emerging through remaining golden-orange foliage
40.childFriendlyNote: The maple colour show is ending. Crunchy leaves pile up ankle-deep on the ground, perfect for stomping through!

40.description: Red oaks among the last trees with colour, deep brown and russet leaves still clinging to branches
40.childFriendlyNote: The stubborn oak leaves hang on and rattle in the wind. They'll be the very last to let go!

40.description: Late goose flocks still passing over, stragglers heading south before freeze-up
40.childFriendlyNote: The last V-formations of geese honk goodbye overhead. They're the slow-coaches heading to warmer places!

40.description: White-throated sparrows still in hedgerows and brush piles, their sweet whistle fading
40.childFriendlyNote: A little stripy bird whistles "Oh sweet Canada, Canada, Canada". Catch the song before they fly south!

40.description: Grey squirrels building leaf nests (dreys) high in bare trees, visible as big balls of leaves in branches
40.childFriendlyNote: See those big messy leaf balls high in the bare trees? Those are squirrel houses, cozy leafy beds for winter!

41.description: Tamarack (larch) trees turning brilliant gold, the only conifer that drops its needles in autumn
41.childFriendlyNote: A tree that looks like a Christmas tree turns gold and drops all its needles! It's the only pine tree that does that

41.description: Juncos settled in for winter, small flocks foraging on ground under feeders and in hedgerows
41.childFriendlyNote: Little grey "snowbirds" hop under the feeder picking up dropped seeds. Where juncos go, snow follows!

41.description: Blue jays still caching acorns, their bright blue plumage vivid against bare grey branches
41.childFriendlyNote: Blue jays shine like blue jewels in the bare grey trees. They're still hiding acorns everywhere!

41.description: Chickadees forming winter flocks with nuthatches and woodpeckers, roving through bare woods together
41.childFriendlyNote: Chickadees team up with other tiny birds for winter. They're like a little gang that travels through the woods together!

41.description: Red squirrels stashing spruce and pine cones in large middens, chattering at intruders
41.childFriendlyNote: Red squirrels pile up cones in a big heap called a midden. It's like their very own pantry for winter!

42.description: Tamarack needles dropping, golden carpet beneath the trees, bare branches revealed
42.childFriendlyNote: The golden tamarack needles fall like soft rain, the only pine tree that goes bald for winter!

42.description: Chickadee winter flocks well established, visiting feeders regularly, caching seeds for later
42.childFriendlyNote: Chickadees hide seeds one by one in bark cracks and remember thousands of hiding spots, smarter than they look!

42.description: Deer in rut, bucks with antlers chasing does, scrapes and rubs visible on trees along forest edges
42.childFriendlyNote: The boy deer have big antlers now and they rub them on trees. Look for scratched-up bark and hoof marks in the mud

42.description: Juncos plentiful at feeders and in leaf litter, a reliable winter presence
42.childFriendlyNote: Little grey birds hop under the feeder picking up dropped seeds. When they fly, their tails flash white like tiny signals!

42.description: Balsam fir trees standing dark green against bare hardwoods, fragrant needles when crushed
42.childFriendlyNote: Squeeze a balsam fir needle and smell. It's like Christmas in your hand! These trees stay green all winter long

43.description: First light snowfalls possible, dusting bare branches and covering fallen leaves: the transition to winter
43.childFriendlyNote: The first snowflakes! Catch one on your tongue or on a dark sleeve. Every single snowflake has a different pattern

43.description: Chickadees visiting feeders in steady stream, mixed flocks working through leafless woodland
43.childFriendlyNote: The brave little chickadee doesn't mind the cold one bit. It puffs up into a fluffy ball to keep warm!

43.description: Deer rut peaking, bucks active during daylight, antler rubs visible on small trees
43.childFriendlyNote: The deer are so busy chasing each other they forget to be careful. You might spot them right in the open!

43.description: Cardinals visiting feeders, bright red males vivid against grey and brown late-autumn landscape
43.childFriendlyNote: The red cardinal looks extra bright now that the leaves are gone, like a ruby in a grey world!

43.description: Red squirrels active all day, defending their cone middens from grey squirrels and blue jays
43.childFriendlyNote: The tiny red squirrel screams at everyone. It doesn't care if you're bigger, this is its food pile!

44.description: Nearly all hardwood trees bare, revealing bird nests, squirrel dreys, and the architecture of branches
44.childFriendlyNote: Now you can see all the secret nests that were hidden by leaves all summer! How many can you count in one tree?

44.description: Chickadees a constant presence at feeders, their "chick-a-dee-dee" call the soundtrack of late autumn
44.childFriendlyNote: A tiny brave bird with a black cap calls its own name: "chick-a-dee-dee-dee!" Count the dees!

44.description: Cardinals at feeders, pairs staying together through winter, the female's warm tawny colour subtle and lovely
44.childFriendlyNote: The red boy cardinal and the brown girl cardinal stick together all winter. They're best friends!

44.description: Blue jays at feeders, bold and noisy, scaring smaller birds away from sunflower seeds
44.childFriendlyNote: The bossy blue jay lands on the feeder and screams "jay! jay!". All the little birds scatter and wait their turn

44.description: Deer rut ending, bucks exhausted, beginning to feed heavily to rebuild strength before deep winter
44.childFriendlyNote: The boy deer are tired from all their chasing. Now they just want to eat and eat to get fat before winter really hits

45.description: First significant snowfalls covering the ground, transforming the landscape to white, fresh animal tracks appearing
45.childFriendlyNote: Real snow! The whole world turns white and quiet. Even the sounds are softer when snow covers everything

45.description: Chickadees fluffed up against cold, visiting feeders in steady rotation with other winter birds
45.childFriendlyNote: The brave little chickadee puffs up into a fluffy ball to keep warm. It weighs less than two nickels!

45.description: Juncos in good numbers under feeders, scratching in leaf litter at woodland edges
45.childFriendlyNote: Little grey birds hop under the feeder picking up dropped seeds. They really do come with the snow!

45.description: White pines standing tall and green against grey sky, soft needles in bundles of five, cones on upper branches
45.childFriendlyNote: White pine needles come in bundles of five, like a tiny hand! Rub them and smell that clean piney scent

45.description: Red cardinals spectacular against fresh white snow, one of winter's most beautiful sights
45.childFriendlyNote: A bright red cardinal on a snowy branch. It looks like the most perfect painting of winter you could ever imagine!

46.description: Downy woodpeckers visiting suet feeders regularly, tapping on branches for hibernating insects
46.childFriendlyNote: Tap-tap-tap! The tiny woodpecker finds bugs hiding under bark. It's like a doctor checking trees with a tiny hammer

46.description: Chickadees taking sunflower seeds one at a time to a branch, holding them with their feet to hammer open
46.childFriendlyNote: Watch the chickadee grab one seed, fly to a branch, and hammer it open with its beak, tap tap tap, then back for more!

46.description: Nuthatches walking headfirst down tree trunks, probing bark crevices for insects and cached seeds
46.childFriendlyNote: This bird walks down the tree headfirst like a little acrobat. No other bird does that!

46.description: Red squirrels retrieving cached cones from middens, chattering angrily if approached
46.childFriendlyNote: The red squirrel digs into its cone pile like a pirate digging up treasure, and growls at anyone who comes near!

46.description: Daylight down to about 9 hours, long blue shadows at midday, sun low on the horizon even at noon
46.childFriendlyNote: It gets dark so early now! Your shadow at lunchtime is as long as a giant's. The sun is barely above the trees

47.description: Pine grosbeaks appearing from the boreal forest in some winters, large rosy finches feeding on mountain ash berries
47.childFriendlyNote: Big rosy-pink birds from the Far North show up to eat berries. They're so tame you can walk right up to them!

47.description: Chickadees feeding in mixed flocks, their calls the most common sound in winter woods
47.childFriendlyNote: A tiny brave bird with a black cap calls its own name: "chick-a-dee-dee-dee!" Count the dees!

47.description: Cardinals visiting feeders at dawn and dusk, red males and tawny females in pairs
47.childFriendlyNote: The reddest bird you ever saw sits on a snowy branch like a little Christmas decoration that stayed behind

47.description: Balsam firs fragrant and green, cones disintegrating on branches releasing winged seeds
47.childFriendlyNote: Squeeze a balsam fir needle between your fingers. It smells exactly like Christmas! These trees stay green all year

47.description: Fresh tracks of foxes, rabbits, and deer telling stories in new snow each morning
47.childFriendlyNote: Snow is like a giant white notebook. Animals write their stories with their feet! Can you tell a fox from a rabbit?

48.description: Blue jays bold and bright at feeders, their blue vivid against white snow and grey sky
48.childFriendlyNote: A bright blue bird with a spiky crest screams "jay jay!" and hogs the feeder. Blue jays are the bullies of the bird world!

48.description: Chickadees lowering their body temperature at night to conserve energy, puffing up by day at feeders
48.childFriendlyNote: The chickadee has a superpower, it makes itself colder at night to save energy, like turning down its own thermostat!

48.description: White pines dusted with snow, long soft needles bowing under the weight, a beautiful winter scene
48.childFriendlyNote: Snow sits on the soft pine branches like fluffy white pillows. Shake one gently and make it snow on yourself!

48.description: Downy woodpeckers at suet feeders and dead branches, small red patch on males visible up close
48.childFriendlyNote: Tap-tap-tap! A little black-and-white bird hammers on a tree like a tiny drummer looking for bugs hiding under bark

48.description: Fox tracks in snow: a neat line of prints, hunting mice by pouncing headfirst into snow
48.childFriendlyNote: A fox hears a mouse under the snow, leaps high in the air, and dives headfirst into the snow to catch it, bonk!

49.description: Chickadees the most reliable winter visitor, calling from every woodland and feeder across the region
49.childFriendlyNote: Hold out your hand with sunflower seeds and stand very still. A chickadee might land right on your fingers!

49.description: Red cardinals striking against winter snow, often the first bird at the feeder at dawn
49.childFriendlyNote: The bright red cardinal is the first one at breakfast. It shows up at the feeder while it's still barely light!

49.description: Large rectangular holes in dead trees from pileated woodpeckers, wood chips piled on snow below
49.childFriendlyNote: A giant woodpecker with a red mohawk smashes square holes in trees. The holes are so big a tennis ball could fit inside!

49.description: Spruce, fir, and pine trees dark green against snow, providing shelter for birds and deer in storms
49.childFriendlyNote: The evergreen forest is like a giant green umbrella in the snow. Deer and birds hide inside when blizzards blow

49.description: Red squirrels active even in bitter cold, retrieving cached food from spruce cone middens
49.childFriendlyNote: Even in a snowstorm, the little red squirrel is out chattering and eating. It never hibernates!

50.description: Chickadees visiting feeders in steady rotation, braving the coldest days with remarkable toughness
50.childFriendlyNote: It's -20 outside but the chickadee doesn't care! It puffs up into a round fluffy ball and keeps singing

50.description: Blue jays retrieving cached acorns from under snow, their memory for hiding spots remarkably good
50.childFriendlyNote: The blue jay remembers where it buried acorns months ago. Even under deep snow! That's a really good memory

50.description: Great horned owls beginning to hoot in early courtship, deep "hoo-hoo-hoooo" calls at dusk
50.childFriendlyNote: At night, a deep "hoo-hoo-hoooo" echoes through the trees. The big owl is starting to think about having babies!

50.description: Shortest days of the year: sunrise after 7:30, sunset before 4:30, deep cold settling in across the region
50.childFriendlyNote: The shortest day of the year! It's dark when you go to school and dark when you come home, but tomorrow the days start getting longer!

50.description: Deer in thick grey winter coats, gathering in sheltered hemlock and cedar stands to ride out storms
50.childFriendlyNote: Deer snuggle together under thick evergreen trees to stay warm. Their hollow winter hairs trap heat like a sleeping bag!

51.description: Chickadees at feeders throughout the day, Canada's favourite winter companion
51.childFriendlyNote: The chickadee weighs about as much as ten paperclips but it survives winters that freeze your nose off!

51.description: Male cardinals brilliant red at feeders against snow, a cheerful holiday-season sight
51.childFriendlyNote: A bright red cardinal on a snowy branch looks just like a Christmas card come to life!

51.description: Great horned owl pairs duetting at dusk, their courtship calls echoing through bare winter woods
51.childFriendlyNote: Two owls hoot back and forth to each other in the dark: the girl's voice is higher and the boy's is deeper!

51.description: Fresh ski and snowshoe tracks through snowy forests, a chance to explore winter woodland at its most magical
51.childFriendlyNote: Strap on snowshoes and walk on top of the deep snow! Everything is quiet and sparkly and your breath makes little clouds

51.description: Fox tracks in fresh snow, a single neat line of prints showing their energy-saving gait
51.childFriendlyNote: Fox footprints make a perfect straight line in the snow. The fox puts its back feet exactly where its front feet stepped!

52.description: Chickadees cheerful at feeders between holiday visits, the most reliable bird of the Canadian winter
52.childFriendlyNote: Even on the coldest day of the year, the chickadee says "chick-a-dee-dee-dee!", the bravest little bird in Canada

52.description: Blue jays noisy at feeders, caching peanuts and sunflower seeds in snow-covered gardens
52.childFriendlyNote: A bright blue bird with a spiky crest screams "jay jay!" and stuffs seeds into its throat pouch like pockets

52.description: Downy woodpeckers at suet feeders, small and perky, often the last birds still feeding as dusk falls
52.childFriendlyNote: Tap-tap-tap! A little black-and-white bird hammers on a tree like a tiny drummer looking for hidden bugs

52.description: Fresh tracks of cottontail rabbits, foxes, and deer telling winter stories in the snow each morning
52.childFriendlyNote: Snow is like a giant white notebook. Animals write their stories with their feet! What visited your garden last night?

52.description: Balsam fir and white spruce standing green and fragrant against deep snow, the heart of the Canadian winter forest
52.childFriendlyNote: Squeeze a balsam fir needle and breathe in. It smells like Christmas! These trees stay green even when everything else is white
